life_summary: George Quincy Morris was born on February 20, 1874, in Salt Lake City, Utah Territory. He grew up in the center of LDS Church activity and received his education in Salt Lake Valley schools. Morris married Emma Ramsey on June 29, 1905, and together they had three daughters: Marian, Margery, and Helen. He established himself as a respected community leader and developed a reputation for sound judgment and spiritual maturity. Morris built a life that balanced family responsibilities with growing involvement in Church leadership at local and regional levels. His journey from lay member to Church leadership reflected his steady growth in spiritual authority and administrative capability over decades of faithful service.
church_summary: Morris served as a missionary in Great Britain from 1899 to 1902. He later served as Superintendent of the Young Men's Mutual Improvement Association (YMMIA) from 1937 to 1948, providing leadership for the Church's youth programs during a critical period. He was called as an Assistant to the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles in 1951 and was ordained as a member of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles in 1954. Morris made Church history by becoming the oldest person to be called to the apostleship, being ordained at the age of eighty. He served in the Quorum of the Twelve from 1954 until his death on April 23, 1962, eight years before his ninetieth birthday.
teaching_emphasis: Age is no barrier to spiritual growth
